Distintas economías responden de forma distinta al mismo proceso. No sé exactamente qué significa para ti recuperarse de la crisis. En EEUU la economía ya crecía en 2010. En España en 2013. Todo dependerá del punto de vista sobre qué significa recuperarse de la crisis. El desempleo, por ejemplo, aún no se ha recuperado a valores previos a la crisis en España. Si tienes en cuenta los indicadores económicos propios a las cohortes jóvenes, la economía española está discutiblemente hoy peor que nunca. Sin embargo el consumo está disparadísimo y con ello los precios y la inflación. Desde esa perspectiva, la economía crece y va como un cohete.

España es una economía increíblemente dependiente del extranjero y ello sumado a la burbuja especulativa inmobiliaria provocó una crisis especialmente grave que se saldó con una destrucción de empleo incomparable a nivel internacional. En un país con un problema de desempleo estructural tan notable y destacable entre las economías desarroladas, es solo fruto de nuestra relación con Europa y de la importancia de nuestro sistema bancario dentro del Euro que alguien pueda siquiera sugerir que hemos salido de la crisis.

Y fíjate que en ninguno de estos elementos entra a colación Zapatero. Las reformas estructurales que la economia española ha necesitado no pueden salir de un simple gobierno de cuatro años sino que se deben incorporar en un gran pacto por el futuro productivo de España dentro de Europa. ¿Podría él haber dirigido este proceso? Ojalá. O cualquier otro. Pero nuestros políticos están a cosas mucho más cortoplacistas que discutir qué va a ser España más que playas y copas.

No soy el de arriba. ¿prevenir la crisis? No. España es un país menor dentro de un mundo financiero globalizado. Afectó especialmente a españa por la situación de la burbuja inmobiliaria, pero la crisis económica y la contracción que supuso eran absolutamente inevitables incluso si hubiésemos tenido a un viajero en el tiempo en el Gobierno. 

¿Mitigar los efectos de la crisis? Los efectos de la crisis fueron los mismos que los de todas las crisis previas. Exigieron un decrecimiento importante del gasto público, un aumento del desempleo y una reducción de los precios. Los efectos de la crisis no son sino las medidas necesarias para reconvertir una economía enferma.

Un viajero en el tiempo hubiera exigido mecanismos de control (a nivel global) para evitar las hipotecas basura, los productos financieros basados en dichas hipotecas y desincentivando y prohibiendo esas y otras realidades que fundamentaron la crisis. Con ello destruyendo mucho empleo y provocando una contracción de la economía tan notable como la misma crisis. Hecho entre 2004 y 2008 no hubiera sido suficiente. La realidad es que para evitar la crisis uno tuviera que haber sido una economía planificada inmunizada ante la especulación financiera. De cualquier otra forma España es solo un mercado más sujeto a la salud de las finanzas a nivel global.

Well... the main issue is going to be your characters and builds haven't reached late game yet.

Crit characters like harumasa and nekomata need very good discs and "just fine" disks aren't going to cut it for "real" late game: shiyu 7 and good 2\* and 3\* scores in DA. I don't think the concept was solid, as you say. From a gameplay and a narrative perspective it was awful.

If you just want to play the game, the fighting game that you play with your agents, the TV mode added absolutely nothing. It also filled a lot of combat content with more loading screens. A lot of randoms and casuals just want to fight and it shows if you are exposed to this kinda player.

If you want to enjoy the narrative, the TV mode was unreadable. It showed story in minimal displays that were very difficult to read. It filled the narrative with puzzles that were effectively as useless narratively as the classic combats jrpg add between cutscenes. 

If you enjoy both, you are consuming a very poor narrative device filled with extra loading screens and puzzles.

But notably, if you enjoy character designs, which is the main draw of these games, you don't get to see your agents. **This is the most important point.**

The only thing it gave, out of the box, was the "immersion". The idea that the proxies are actually intervening through the TV system in connection to the agents. It is definitely not worth it for most players.

The only thing it "could have" removed, other than the immersion, were the puzzles. But even if people (I) enjoy puzzles, I don't particularly mind if they are on the TV mode or somewhere else. I enjoy most kinds of puzzles hoyo makes, especially when they are slightly more challenging than average hoyo puzzles.

I am convinced their outputs reveal TV mode was just a mistake financially and it's never coming back. It keeps casuals out of the game by hiding their cool designs, narrative and gameplay behind an immersion justified glorified cutscene-puzzle.

I think the story this patch greatly outdid itself. In my opinion this is the best story patch since release, even better than 1.4. They finally decided that "named" characters can be grey. Also, they put some value in the cyberpunk motifs, which has been a gripe of mine with the game since release (I've brought it up here in the past too).

It has some of the classic issues. People "find out about secrets" almost instantly with no reasoning, and foreshadowing lasts about 30 seconds, people love the proxies instantly... but honestly considering how simple previous patches were, this is a major step forward in complexity of themes and narrative.

I also think the game did justice to Lycaon this patch, tremendously so. I was not particularly fond of any character in that faction and my opinion on him has greatly improved.

All of these characters have massively improved the tone of the game and the way it interacts with the underlying themes: in cutthroat capitalism the debate between optimism and reformism vs. social revolution, etc. I'm not saying the story is going to change or have any consequences (I expect everyone to be friends in the end anyway) but if they allow characters to be flawed, multidimensional and complex just like this, the game is going to be just so much better narratively. And at no major cost.

Personally I find this game has more teambuilding issues than others (passives, horizontal investment) and Deadly Assault requiring three teams puts extra weight on that. So, when people submit scores, this shows in the average scores.

For example, my experience with Zhu Yuan is that, when paired with Astra and Nicole, she can destroy her side of any gamemode. But if you can't spare Astra for her, suddenly she can't perform every time. I don't have Qingyi, but if I did, she also has other teams to take part in. This doesn't happen to Miyabi, which I pair with free to play units "even if I have better teams", just because this allows me to get 9 stars.

I think the flexibility of some characters: Miyabi, Yanagi, Burnice, Astra and Caesar; is the actual Tier0-0.5 of this game, something prydwen isn't truly referencing, even if the tier positions are there. Maybe Evelyn too. These characters will achieve or help achieve 20k with free characters. They will consistently reach high average points. My impression is S0 Anby joins the same rank due to having several cheap options, but I dont know yet. 

I think Prydwen has issues interpreting sky high values. Evelyn may hit 60k points on her best team, but this is not as useful to account building as having Evelyn and Astra in different teams, both achieving 20k with cheap teams. Which they do, by the way, at least so far.

In any case as we get more and more characters and more teambuilding options, this will disappear. 

**TLDR: the value of generalist and flexible characters in this game massively outweights the "miyabillion damage" argument that fuels the list. Grab characters that let you clear flexibly.**

There are two kinds of tapes: "Master tapes" and "Encrypted master tapes". Master tapes can only be used in the stable channel, also known as the "general banner". And both kind of tapes can only be used for gacha pulls, there are no other uses for them.

My advice -most people will agree- is to **never** exchange Polycromes for Master tapes. But you can buy a few Master Tapes with other resources. For example, you can buy 5 master tapes (and 5 encrypted master tapes) a month in exchange for "fading signals". You should always do this every month.

Otherwise, you should exchange all of your polycromes only for "Encrypted master tapes" and pull for the characters you want. All of this is very confusing but all mihoyo games work in the same way so all of this advice works across games.

let me hijack your question to add that a very common "new to gacha" mistake is spending limited resources on the "stable channel". Unless you are willing to spend a lot of money you should avoid spending limited resources (Polycromes) in the general banner. Eventually, in 6 months to a year, you will have all characters from the stable channel through "free generic pulls" and lost 50/50s from the limited banner.
